references.text: The immediate context: the earth was corrupt and full of violence (חָמָס), which is the direct justification for God's judgment in verse 13.
God elaborates on His decision from verse 13 by explaining that He will bring a flood upon the earth to destroy all flesh that has the breath of life.
The prophet Ezekiel uses similar expressions: 'The end has come' (קֵץ בָּא), which reflects God's words in Genesis 6:13 that 'the end of all flesh has come before Me'.

Noah's faith is described: he was warned by God about what had not yet been seen (the coming flood), and in reverence he built the ark to save his household – a direct response to God's announcement in Genesis 6:13.

Peter points out that God did not spare the ancient world, but preserved Noah and seven others when He brought the flood upon the world of the ungodly – a direct reference to God's judgment in Genesis 6:13.

Peter mentions the days of Noah when God waited patiently while the ark was being built, and only eight souls were saved through water – a reference to the flood that God warned Noah about in Genesis 6:13.

The destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah: the angels say they will destroy the place because the outcry against it has become great – a parallel to God's judgment over violence and wickedness in Genesis 6:13.
Theological parallel: God turning His face away as a precondition for complete destruction.
Theological parallel: Judgment on human sin affects all creation (humans, animals, nature).
Theological parallel: Judgment on human sin affects both humans and animals.
Theological parallel: Total destruction of the earth as a result of human sin.
Theological parallel: Global judgment over all nations and the earth because of sin.
Theological parallel: Sin leads to self-destruction, and God's wrath is poured out on deeds.
Theological parallel: 'The end' has come as a result of God's patience running out.
Theological parallel: God's judgment falls upon an entire group because of sin and rebellion.
Theological parallel: Judgment on human sin affects both humans and animals.
Theological parallel: The earth bears witness to human violence and is struck by judgment.
Theological parallel: God's judgment on those who destroy the earth because of sin.
Theological parallel: God's appointed destruction over the whole earth due to sin.
Theological parallel: God's judgment on the earth is based on justice.
Theological parallel: God's wrath as a response to human sin and injustice.
Theological parallel: God's eradication of the wicked because of their evil.
Theological parallel: The day of the Lord that destroys the earth and wipes out sinners.
Theological parallel: God's judgment on the nations that fill the earth with corpses.
Theological parallel: God's hand is stretched out against a sinful land, destroying both people and animals.
Theological parallel: God's case against the peoples and judgment upon all flesh.
